own_solution.law: With the initial passing point as the origin, x_truck = vt and x_car = (1/2)at². Their next meeting occurs at t = 2v/a = 15 s. A kit fitted to the car for this chase changes its acceleration to a + q, giving t = 30/(2 + q) s. For q = 0.6, 1.3 and 2.5 m/s², the times are respectively 11.5384615, 9.0909091 and 6.6666667 s.
assumptions: Use Newtonian motion along the stated straight road.
The requested meeting occurs after the initial passing.
The car's acceleration remains constant, including the kit's increment when fitted for this chase.
The kit used for an earlier run only has no effect on the present run.

notes: All certified answers, dependency claims and units are correct. Both declared minimal pairs preserve 1.3 m/s² and change the intended attachment: another object or an earlier event versus the car in the present chase. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering objection because pass 2 explicitly identifies T0812 and TB52F as numeral-free controls, rather than claiming they preserve the numerical content of the minimal pairs. Their stated numeral-free transformations are accurate. All supplied information was contained in the message; no tools or external information were used.
